title: Adaptive handoff bridge for AsyncIterator <-> Web Streams with resumable checkpoints
creator: Ravi Patel
acceptance_criteria: Adapter exposes asAsyncIterator() and asReadableStream() and they can be used interchangeably in simple examples
Cancellation propagates in both directions in Node, browser, and Deno environments
Resumable checkpoint tokens are emitted and lastCheckpoint() returns the latest emitted token
Backpressure mechanism prevents unbounded memory growth in stress tests (verify with high-throughput synthetic harness)
Tee/clone helper produces independent branches and per-branch checkpointing
Comprehensive unit tests and E2E integration tests with node-fetch and cross-fetch in browsers/Deno
tasks: implement core adapter and seq/checkpoint metadata (3 days)
add backpressure waterline primitives and defaults (2 days)
implement tee() and per-branch checkpointing (2 days)
write unit tests + platform compatibility tests (3 days)
create examples + docs and migration guide (1 day)
test_plan: Unit tests: cover sync/async producers, iterator.return() -> stream.cancel() and reverse. Platform matrix: Node 18+, Deno latest, Chrome/Firefox. Integration: wire adapter to a small local test server that supports resume tokens. Stress: synthetic harness that pushes > 1000 small chunks/sec for 60s and verify memory stable. Network resilience: inject transient network failures and verify resume behavior when server honors token and graceful fallback when not supported.
